Title: Access admin-only UI route without being a multisig signer
How to test: Navigate directly to the admin/config URL with a non-signer wallet connected
Expected Result: Route either redirects/hides admin controls, and any admin action attempted from it is rejected on-chain (not just hidden by the front end)

Title: Call read-only API for another wallet's data without authorization
How to test: Using DevTools/curl, request the API endpoint with an arbitrary wallet address that is not the connected one
Expected Result: API returns data (by design, if truly read-only/public) or is explicitly rejected — verify the response matches the intended access model, not an accidental broader leak (e.g. internal fields, other users' PII)

Title: Bypass "connect wallet" gate to reach staking actions
How to test: Try to open the Stake/Claim/Unstake screens directly via URL without connecting a wallet
Expected Result: Screens either require connection before allowing any signable action, or any attempt to build/sign a transaction fails gracefully

Title: Submit stake instruction referencing a different wallet as the position owner (IDOR)
How to test: Copy the stake request from the Network tab, replace the "owner"/"authority" account with a victim wallet's pubkey, sign with the attacker's key and submit
Expected Result: Program rejects the transaction (owner/authority must match signer) — stake is not created against the victim's PDA

Title: Submit claim instruction for a position owned by another wallet
How to test: Modify the intercepted claim transaction to target another user's known position PDA while signing as attacker
Expected Result: Program rejects the instruction because the signer is not the authority on that position account

Title: Submit unstake instruction for a position PDA belonging to another wallet
How to test: Modify the intercepted unstake transaction's position account to a victim's PDA, keep attacker as signer
Expected Result: Program rejects the instruction
column4: victim's funds are not withdrawn to the attacker

Title: Attempt daily check-in on a position owned by another wallet
How to test: Modify the intercepted check-in transaction to reference another user's position while signing as attacker
Expected Result: Program rejects the check-in

Title: Attempt to redirect claim/unstake payout to an arbitrary destination account
How to test: Edit the destination token account in the intercepted transaction to an attacker-controlled ATA that isn't derived from the position owner
Expected Result: Program validates the destination account is the owner's associated token account (or explicit owner check) and rejects mismatched destinations

Title: Race two simultaneous stakes near the global cap boundary
How to test: From two wallets, submit stakes simultaneously that would jointly push total staked just over the 30,000,000 MEX global cap
Expected Result: Only stakes that keep the total at or under the cap succeed
column4: the one that would exceed it is rejected (note: currently unenforced per PRD — expect this to fail until implemented)

Title: Race two simultaneous stakes near the per-wallet cap boundary
How to test: From the same wallet, fire two stake transactions concurrently that would jointly exceed the 500,000 MEX per-wallet cap
Expected Result: Only the portion within the cap succeeds
column4: the excess is rejected (note: currently unenforced per PRD — expect this to fail until implemented)

Title: Race claim and compound on the same position
How to test: Trigger "Claim" and "Compound" on the same position at nearly the same time (two browser tabs / two quick clicks)
Expected Result: Only one action succeeds per reward unit
column4: rewards are not paid out twice (no double accrual/double spend)

Title: Race two unstake requests on the same position
How to test: Submit two unstake transactions for the same position in quick succession
Expected Result: Only the first succeeds
column4: the second fails because the position account no longer exists/has no funds (no double withdrawal)

Title: Race two check-ins on the same position within the same day
How to test: Send two check-in transactions back-to-back for the same position
Expected Result: Only one check-in per day is recorded

Title: Race check-in and unstake on a position at unlock time
How to test: Submit a check-in and an unstake instruction for the same position at the moment it unlocks
Expected Result: Both resolve consistently with the documented order of operations
column4: no state where rewards are lost or duplicated

Title: Bypass front-end minimum stake amount
How to test: Intercept the stake request, lower the amount below the UI-enforced minimum, sign and submit directly
Expected Result: Program-level minimum (if any) rejects the amount, or if there is no on-chain minimum this is flagged as a gap between UI and contract validation

Title: Bypass front-end per-wallet cap check via crafted instruction
How to test: Build/submit a stake instruction directly (bypassing the UI form) for an amount that would exceed the 500,000 MEX per-wallet cap
Expected Result: Program rejects the excess amount (currently expected to fail since the cap isn't implemented on-chain per PRD)

Title: Bypass front-end global cap check via crafted instruction
How to test: Build/submit a stake instruction directly for an amount that would push total pool stake over 30,000,000 MEX
Expected Result: Program rejects the excess amount (currently expected to fail since the cap isn't implemented on-chain per PRD)

Title: Bypass "already checked in today" UI lock
How to test: Directly resend the check-in instruction from Network tab multiple times within the same day, bypassing the disabled button
Expected Result: Program rejects check-ins beyond one per day regardless of UI state

Title: Bypass "locked, cannot unstake" UI restriction
How to test: Directly submit the unstake instruction copied from Network tab for a position still within its lock window
Expected Result: Program rejects the unstake based on on-chain lock-end timestamp, independent of what the UI allowed to be built

Title: Submit a zero-amount stake instruction
How to test: Craft and submit a stake transaction with amount = 0
Expected Result: Program rejects zero-amount stakes with a clear error, no position/account is created

Title: Submit a negative or overflow amount for stake
How to test: Craft a stake instruction with a negative (if representable) or numerically overflowing amount value
Expected Result: Program rejects the malformed amount
column4: no unexpected large balance is credited

Title: Submit a stake instruction with amount exceeding wallet's actual MEX balance
How to test: Craft a stake transaction requesting more MEX than the wallet holds, submit directly
Expected Result: Transaction fails at the token-transfer level (insufficient funds)

Title: Tamper with displayed APR/rate value client-side and attempt to claim based on it
How to test: Use DevTools to modify the rendered rate/APR value, then trigger claim
Expected Result: Actual paid-out amount is computed and enforced by the program from on-chain state, not from the tampered display value

Title: Attempt to skip wallet's signature by replaying a pre-approved transaction payload
How to test: Capture a previously built (unsigned) transaction payload from the Network tab and attempt to resubmit it without a fresh signature
Expected Result: Submission fails without a valid, matching signature from the required signer

Title: Access the indexer's internal/administrative endpoints if exposed
How to test: Enumerate API routes found in the front-end bundle/Network tab for anything beyond the documented read-only endpoints
Expected Result: No write/administrative capability is exposed on endpoints that are supposed to be read-only

Title: Check for sensitive data exposure in front-end bundle or API responses
How to test: Search the JS bundle and API responses (via DevTools) for private keys, admin secrets, or internal service URLs
Expected Result: No secrets/keys beyond what's required for public RPC access are present in client-visible code or responses

Title: Attempt cross-wallet session confusion by switching Phantom account mid-session
How to test: Connect wallet A, open a position's action modal, switch Phantom to wallet B without reloading, then submit
Expected Result: The app either forces a reload/reconnect flow or correctly rebuilds the transaction for the newly active wallet B (no action is silently signed/attributed to the wrong wallet)

Title: Verify client-side validation errors have matching on-chain enforcement for every blocked action found above
How to test: For each case where the UI blocks an action, also attempt the equivalent raw instruction via DevTools-copied request
Expected Result: Every UI-side restriction has an equivalent on-chain check
column4: any UI-only restriction is logged as a bug (front end is a hint, program is the source of truth)
